articles.title: João Merín faz 'Sinfonia de reis' com Thalma de Freitas em álbum autoral em que reúne Max B.O. e Rincon Sapiência | G1
articles.body:
Capa do álbum 'Meninos brincando na lua', do rapper baiano João Merín — Foto: Ciberdelia

♬ Antecedido pelo single “Céu de setembro”, lançado em 9 de setembro, o quarto álbum do rapper baiano João Merín, “Meninos brincando na lua”, aterrissa nos aplicativos de áudio em 27 de setembro – dia dos santos gêmeos Cosme & Damião – em edição do selo Curruíra.

Com dez músicas, o álbum “Meninos brincando na lua” apresenta repertório autoral composto por Merín com Yaan e Yky Castilho, produtores musicais do álbum. O rap é o ponto de partida para o cantor e compositor – nascido e criado em Salvador (BA), terra de gêneros como ijexá e samba-reggae – inserir elementos de música erudita, afrobeats, ritmos afro-baianos e música eletrônica no universo do hip hop.

Com participações de Rincon Sapiência , Thalma de Freitas, Max B.O. e Carol Mathias, o álbum “Meninos brincando na lua” sucede os álbuns “Yat” (2019), “Os últimos filhos de Sião” (2020) e “Galo, a ciência do tambor” (2022) na discografia solo de João Merín, iniciada há sete anos.

Rincon Sapiência figura na música “Viramar”, de cuja letra é coautor em parceria com Merín. Thalma de Freitas faz feat com João Merín em “Sinfonia dos reis”. Já Max B.O. e Carol Mathias se juntam com Yky Castilho na faixa “Onde o céu desaba”.

Outras músicas do álbum “Meninos brincando na lua” são “Amoras”, “Ensaio para o adeus” – gravada com o sopro da flauta de Vinicius Chagas – e “O que sobrou de nois ”.

articles.title: 1º Festival do Café de Varre-Sai reúne atrações culturais | G1
articles.standfirst: Evento acontece de sexta-feira (18) a domingo (20), com atrações musicais, produtores locais, gastronomia e atividades voltadas à cafeicultura.
articles.summary: Evento acontece de sexta-feira (18) a domingo (20), com atrações musicais, produtores locais, gastronomia e atividades voltadas à cafeicultura.
articles.body:
Área de eventos recebe os preparativos para o 1º Festival do Café de Varre-Sai. — Foto: Diego Varsi

Neste fim de semana, Varre-Sai , no Noroeste Fluminense, recebe o 1º Festival do Café. O evento, realizado na área de eventos do município, terá programação dedicada à valorização da produção cafeeira local e à homenagem a produtores, meeiros e trabalhadores do setor.

A programação tem como destaques o 1º Concurso Rainha do Café, nesta sexta-feira (18), às 19h, e o show do grupo Falamansa, às 22h. No sábado (19), também às 22h, quem sobe ao palco é a cantora Mari Fernandez. O festival terá ainda apresentações de Erica Carvalho, Suate e Bira Bello.

Sete candidatas, representando diferentes comunidades rurais de Varre-Sai, participam da disputa. Antonella representa a comunidade Barra Funda; Rafaela, Morro da Máquina; Bernadete, Arataca; Isabelly, Prata; Isabela e Eliza representam Jacutinga; e Laryssa, a comunidade Santa Lúcia.

Além do concurso, a programação conta com a 1ª Mostra de Café Torrado, estandes de produtores locais, gastronomia, exposições e gincanas.

O festival segue até domingo (20), reunindo atividades culturais e de valorização de uma das principais atividades econômicas do município.

articles.title: Confira programação do Festival de Verão Salvador 2027 | G1
articles.standfirst: Evento será realizado nos dias 23 e 24 de janeiro, na Arena Festival, no Wet Eventos, em Salvador.
articles.summary: Evento será realizado nos dias 23 e 24 de janeiro, na Arena Festival, no Wet Eventos, em Salvador. Programação terá encontro exclusivo de Timbalada e Olodum.
articles.body:
Festival de Verão 2027 terá encontro exclusivo de Timbalada e Olodum; Péricles, Marina Sena e mais completam grade de atrações — Foto: Divulgação/Marithê do Céu/Reprodução/Tácio Moreira/Macaco Gordo/Divulgação

O Festival de Verão Salvador anunciou, nesta sexta-feira (18), a grade de atrações da 26ª edição do evento. O festival será realizado nos dias 23 e 24 de janeiro, na Arena Festival, no Wet Eventos, e terá nomes de diferentes gerações e estilos da música brasileira.

As atrações são: Maria Bethânia, Gilsons, BaianaSystem com IZA, Gilsons, “O Grande Encontro", formado por Elba Ramalho, Alceu Valença e Geraldo Azevedo, “As Vozes”, projeto de Péricles e Ferrugem, É o Tchan, Marina Sena, João Gomes, Saulo e o encontro entre Timbalada e Olodum.

Segundo a organização, duas atrações que vão se apresentar no domingo (24) ainda serão anunciadas. As informações foram divulgadas pela Bahia Eventos e Salvador Produções, que realizam juntas a produção do evento.

O show de Timbalada & Olodum foi criado especialmente para o festival e reunirá as duas formações no palco durante toda a apresentação. A proposta é combinar os tambores e o samba-reggae dos dois grupos, que têm trajetórias marcantes na música produzida em Salvador.

Outro encontro anunciado é o de BaianaSystem e IZA. O grupo baiano levará para o palco sua mistura de guitarra baiana, sound system e referências da música afro-baiana, enquanto a cantora apresenta elementos do pop, R&B e reggae.

Maria Bethânia chega ao festival após celebrar seis décadas de carreira. Já “O Grande Encontro” reúne Alceu Valença, Elba Ramalho e Geraldo Azevedo em um espetáculo baseado em ritmos como frevo, baião, maracatu e ciranda.

No projeto “As Vozes”, Péricles e Ferrugem dividem o palco durante todo o show, com um repertório que aproxima o samba e o pagode de diferentes gerações.

O grupo baiano É o Tchan representa o pagode baiano, com sucessos que marcaram a trajetória do grupo e coreografias que fazem parte da identidade da banda. Já Saulo apresenta músicas de diferentes fases da carreira, incluindo faixas do álbum “Bênção”.

Marina Sena leva ao festival a fase do álbum “Coisas Naturais”, terceiro trabalho de estúdio da cantora, lançado em 2025. João Gomes, por sua vez, apresenta sucessos como “Meu Pedaço de Pecado”, “Dengo” e “Eu Tenho a Senha”, além de músicas de outras fases da carreira.

O Gilsons, formado por José Gil, Francisco Gil e João Gil, retorna ao Festival de Verão depois de ter sido anunciado como a primeira atração da edição de 2027 durante um pocket show surpresa na edição de 2026.

Em entrevista ao g1 , o diretor artístico do Festival de Verão Salvador, Zé Ricardo, destacou o desafio de montar a programação em um estado com uma produção cultural intensa e diversa. Segundo ele, a curadoria busca renovar a identidade do evento a cada edição, sem deixar de valorizar a cena musical baiana.

"Montar um line-up do Festival de Verão é uma honra. É uma dificuldade, porque a Bahia é uma cultura que pulsa o ano inteiro, principalmente em janeiro, quando a gente tem tanta oferta de cultura maravilhosa, tantos artistas, não só baianos, mas que vêm do Brasil inteiro para cá. Então, é um desafio, é uma busca muito profunda de tentar provocar, tentar trazer novas ideias, tentar ressignificar o Festival a cada edição. Mas, no final das contas, é uma grande honra poder trabalhar na Bahia", afirmou Zé Ricardo, diretor artístico do Festival de Verão Salvador.

articles.title: Kim Kardashian's esophagitis diagnosis raises concerns over dad's death
articles.summary: Kim Kardashian's esophagitis diagnosis prompted an emotional reaction from her mother, Kris Jenner, due to the death of Robert Kardashian Sr.
articles.body:
A recent diagnosis for Kim Kardashian is worrying her inner circle.

In a Sept. 17 trailer for Season 8 of "The Kardashians," the Skims founder, 45, is diagnosed with esophagitis. The condition involves inflammation of the esophagus, according to the Mayo Clinic .

The trailer, which did not detail the severity of Kardashian's diagnosis, shows that the diagnosis prompted concern from friends and family. Kim's late father, Robert Kardashian, died at age 59 in 2003 after battling esophageal cancer, a condition distinct from esophagitis.

"I have something called esophagitism," she said in the teaser while getting her hair done. The trailer then shows the reality TV star in a hospital bed undergoing a medical examination, while an off-camera voice asks: "Didn't your father… isn't it what he died of?"

"I can't, it makes me want to cry," Kris Jenner said as she reacts to her daughter's diagnosis.

Robert Kardashian and Jenner welcomed Kim in 1980, as well as Kourtney, 47, Khloé, 42, and Rob Jr., 39. Robert Kardashian Sr. was an attorney and businessman best known for representing former NFL player O.J. Simpson during his highly publicized murder trial.

According to the Mayo Clinic, esophagitis is a "swelling and irritation, called inflammation, of the tissues that line the esophagus. The esophagus is the muscular tube that carries food and drink from the mouth to the stomach.

The inflammation can make swallowing difficult or painful and can also cause chest pain, the clinic says. Esophagitis can be caused by several factors, including stomach acid backing up into the esophagus, infection, allergies, and oral medications.

Treatment varies depending on its cause and the severity of tissue damage in the esophagus.

As the esophagus struggles to move food and liquid from the mouth to the stomach, the condition can cause dehydration, unhealthy weight loss, scarring or narrowing of the esophagus, or other serious health concerns, according to the Mayo Clinic.

From Lena Dunham to Kim Kardashian, see the celebs who had children via surrogacy

Lena Dunham revealed on Sept. 16 that she and husband, Luis Felber , welcomed their first child together, a baby daughter, via surrogate. See other celebrities who have also welcomed children through surrogacy and spoken about their journies.

Esophageal cancer is when cancerous cells in the esophagus multiply and create tumors.

According to the Cleveland Clinic , symptoms of esophageal cancer are not always present in the early stages. When they do occur, symptoms can include difficulty swallowing, weight loss, heartburn, and hoarseness.

Other symptoms include heartburn, chest pain, vomiting, coughing up blood, or pain in the throat, back, behind the breastbone, or between the shoulder blades.

The Cleveland Clinic states there are two types of esophageal cancer, including the more common in the United States, adenocarcinoma, which develops in tissue that makes mucus to help people swallow and typically impacts the lower part of the esophagus.

The other is squamous cell carcinoma, which starts in the squamous cells that line the esophagus and affects the upper and middle parts of the esophagus, according to the Cleveland Clinic.

articles.title: Asian Influencer Earning $1 Million A Year Says She’s Quitting To Become A Doctor: “I Think Being An Influencer Is Harder Than Being A Doctor”
articles.summary: Reyna Nguyen is moving away from content creation to pursue a career in dermatology, even though it requires a significant pay cut. Nguyen always dreamt of b...
articles.body:
Influencer Reyna Nguyen is leaving her $1 million a year career to pursue her dream of becoming a dermatologist, citing the desire for a more stable and meaningful life.

Nguyen, who majored in bioengineering with a premedical focus, plans to integrate her passion for skin with science and technology in her future medical career.

Despite the financial uncertainty and instability of entrepreneurship, Nguyen is willing to take a pay cut to practice medicine, aiming to contribute more meaningfully and make a bigger difference in people's lives.

Reyna Nguyen is moving away from content creation to pursue a career in dermatology, even though it requires a significant pay cut.

Nguyen always dreamt of becoming a doctor and majored in bioengineering with a premedical focus at the university. However, she abandoned those plans to become financially independent more quickly and took on content creation instead.

Now, after several years of building her online career, she is ready to return to the field she originally intended to join, though this means giving up some flexibility and potentially the income she currently earns.

"I think being an influencer is harder than being a doctor," Nguyen said. "It's a different type of work, but I think they're both really hard."

Nguyen works between 10 and 14 hours a day, balancing content creation, social media, administration, management, and other aspects of running her online career. Her daily tasks include making multiple TikToks, coordinating with assistants and management teams, planning content, organizing shoots, and creating paid content.

"Every day is so different," she said. "Last week, I had to fly my assistant over because we just had so much to do."

"I would wake up, get ready, and then I have to make 20 TikTok videos, and they all have to be new. Then it's admin work, checking emails, talking to assistants and management. Then planning the content day and actually setting up for each piece of content."

What makes Nguyen's career different from medicine, she says, is not the amount of work but its instability.

"I don't think [being a doctor] is going to be more relaxing, but I think it'll be more stable, which is something I don't really have right now," she says.

The unpredictability of being an entrepreneur makes financial planning rather challenging for Nguyen.

"We have months where we do really well and months where we don't do really well," she said. "One of the most frustrating things for me is financial planning because I don't know how much longer I can do this job for."

"You're stuck in this phase of being in panic constantly because you're like, 'Okay, I don't know when this money is going to run out. How can I make sure I have enough to live a stable life?'"

This makes Nguyen's choice even more understandable since she decided to return to medicine. As for her specialization, Nguyen has always been interested in skin, so she wants to become a dermatologist, combining her passion for skin with the science and technology she was originally drawn to.

"I've always wanted to be a doctor because I really like helping people," she said. "I wanted to specifically go into dermatology because I love skin and I love how it incorporates science and technology, which is what I was studying in college anyway."

Nguyen had also shadowed doctors and liked it.

"I shadowed doctors, and I loved it," she recalled. "It was great."

Pursuing medicine means several years of education and further residency, but Nguyen said she is ready to face it.

"I'm already working so much nowadays that the residency and fellowships won't be an issue for me," she said. "I'm already working 12- to 14-hour days."

For Nguyen, switching to such a regulated, structured job will be easier.

"My life now is so chaotic. Every day is a new day. Something else is going on," she said. "As a doctor, you take the knowledge you already have and apply it every single day. It's more routine."

Nguyen said she currently earns around $1 million a year, so switching to medicine means accepting lower pay unless she practices in the United States. She also mentioned that certain specializations in the U.S. can provide the same pay over time.

"If I practice in Australia, I'd definitely take a pay cut, but if I practice in America, it could probably be about the same, honestly," she says.

Money isn't what matters to her in the first place. One thing she is waiting for in the future is the ability to speak freely about her job in front of her family and feel that what she does makes a bigger difference in other people's lives.

"I look forward to being able to be entirely open about what I do with my family," she says.

"It would be nice to contribute more meaningfully and change people's lives," she adds. "Do some good in the world."

Nguyen has wondered whether her past in the online world would influence her future in medicine, especially if patients or colleagues ever learned about her history. However, after talking to doctors who were interviewing medical candidates, she was relieved.

"I talked to some of my doctor friends who have hosted interviews for applicants, and I was talking about what angle I should use," she said. "They just said, 'Ignore it. Talk about the startups, talk about how you own the business.'"

Nguyen sees her long-term goal in integrating medicine with entrepreneurship rather than working as a traditional physician.

"If I own my own practice, my plan wouldn't be to work there every single day," she said. "It would be to open up a business and then come in two or three times a week to help and manage."

Nguyen noted that switching to medicine is not about shying away from hard work. It is about creating a life that is more stable and meaningful.

"I don't think it's going to be more relaxing," she said. "But I think it'll be more stable."

articles.title: Bugatti Refuses To Sell Parts to YouTuber Who Fixed a $1.2 Million Veyron for $54
articles.summary: If there is one person currently keeping the executives at Bugatti awake at night, it is Mat Armstrong. Over the last year, the British YouTuber has single-h...
articles.body:
If there is one person currently keeping the executives at Bugatti awake at night, it is Mat Armstrong. Over the last year, the British YouTuber has single-handedly dismantled the myth that maintaining a modern hypercar requires a team of factory-certified, white-gloved engineers.

His latest automotive conquest is an incredibly rare, 1-of-1 Oakley Design Bugatti Veyron tuned to 1,200 horsepower. The car was sitting dead in the back of a Dubai showroom with massive start faults and gearbox issues. Because the local dealer network wouldn't touch it without an exorbitant blank check, Armstrong bought the non-running hypercar for roughly $1.2 million, shipped it to the UK, and fixed the car's most catastrophic issues for a grand total of $54 , using cheap submersible fuel hoses and a $14 ignition switch ripped out of a Volkswagen Transporter.

But as Armstrong continues to dial in the Oakley Design Veyron on his second channel, Mat Armstrong MK2 , the hypercar manufacturer is officially pushing back.

With the Veyron fully running and driving, Armstrong turned his attention to standard maintenance, noting that the front AP Racing brake pads were getting dangerously thin. But when he tried to source replacements through the official dealer network, Bugatti flat-out refused the sale.

"We called our parts guy who gets the parts from Bugatti; they won't sell them to us because they need a special bedding-in procedure which needs to be done at Bugatti apparently," Armstrong explained.

The restriction is a classic "right to repair" blockade, forcing owners to rely exclusively on the factory for basic consumable maintenance. And that factory service comes with an absolutely nauseating luxury tax. The widely circulated dealership quote for replacing Veyron brake pads front and rear sits around £50,000.

Armstrong's response? He bypassed the dealer network entirely and found a brand new set online for a fraction of the cost.

"£50,000 is just made-up nonsense that is utter rubbish," he scoffed. "I've got a new set for £1,500".

While waiting for the rogue brake pads to ship from America, Armstrong treated the Veyron to a backyard oil change—a process that perfectly highlights how needlessly complicated hypercar engineering can be.

Because the massive W16 engine utilizes a dry-sump lubrication system with multiple oil catchments to prevent starvation during high-speed cornering, draining the fluid requires pulling a ridiculous amount of hardware. "There was 16 sump plugs," Armstrong laughed as he crawled under the carbon-fiber undertray.

He also continued hunting down the source of an annoying airbag warning light on the dashboard. After tracing the circuit to a melted pyrofuse connection in the battery compartment, he discovered that the highly sensitive, hypercar-exclusive electrical connector was actually just a parts-bin crossover from a Volkswagen Touareg and a Porsche Cayenne.

Of course, the Veyron isn't the only headache in the Armstrong garage right now.

While upgrading the crank hub on his BMW M3 F80 build (jokingly referred to as the "million horsepower" project), disaster struck when a drill bit cleanly snapped off directly inside the engine block template.

Even worse, Armstrong revealed a massive financial loss regarding his infamous neon-green Mercedes C63 AMG. After deciding to cut his losses on the poorly-fitting Black Series replica, he sold it to a breaker's yard for £9,000, assuming it would be stripped for parts. Instead, the yard flipped the severely faulty car to an unsuspecting buyer who took out loans to purchase it. Out of guilt, Armstrong stepped in to protect the buyer and bought the broken car back.

"I've had to buy the car back for £15,000, which makes me at a six-grand loss for a car that is actually worse now," he admitted.

Despite the C63 loss, Armstrong is sitting on an absolute goldmine with the Bugatti. After running a complete CarVertical background check and confirming the Oakley Design Veyron had zero accident history, he brought the car to luxury dealer Carl Hartley for an appraisal.

Hartley valued the tuned 1-of-1 hypercar at a staggering £1.5 million (roughly $2 million USD). Armstrong actually thinks it could push higher, but either way, he is hundreds of thousands of dollars in the green.

"If you told me what had happened this year… if you told me that there'd be two Veyrons that I've worked on, never let alone owned, I would never have believed you," he reflected, looking at the two Bugattis sitting side-by-side in his shop.

articles.title: Joe Rogan calls Trump supporters 'nuts' after 2024 endorsement
articles.summary: Podcast megastar Joe Rogan said he has been left-leaning throughout his life and called Donald Trump supporters 'nuts' in a recent podcast appearance.
articles.body:
Podcaster Joe Rogan said he has been left-wing for most of his life and called President Donald Trump 's supporters "nuts" and "rabid."

Rogan endorsed Trump in the 2024 election after the candidate appeared on his podcast, which is often considered part of the "manosphere" that helped buoy Trump's reelection bid. Rogan has spoken out about parts of the second Trump presidency, like mass deportations and the war in Iran , but still appeared as a commentator at the Freedom 250 UFC Fight Night at the White House.

Speaking with comedian and actor Ron White in an episode that aired Sept. 16, Rogan seemed to distance himself from the president's fanbase. From his studio in Austin, Texas, he said he liked Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate James Talarico , running against Ken Paxton. They also laughed at country star Jelly Roll's recent jokes about Trump . Here is what he had to say:

Trump's naming campaign, from the Kennedy Center to Trump RX

From Lake America to buildings and institutions bearing Trump's name, see the places, landmarks and public spaces tied to the president's branding campaign. Pictured here, a map labeling Lake Ontario as " Lake America " is displayed as President Donald Trump signs an executive order to rename Lake Ontario as "Lake America" on Aug. 27, 2026, amid an ongoing trade war between the U.S. and Canada. See what Trump has renamed or attached his name to.

Joe Rogan says he has been 'left-wing my whole life'

Rogan and White were talking about critiques of Comedy Mothership , Rogan's comedy club in Austin, Texas. Rogan said people assumed the entire club leaned right-wing because of his association with it. Plus, Comedian Tony Hinchcliffe , who caused controversy at a 2024 Trump campaign rally at Madison Square Garden, tapes his weekly "Kill Tony" show at the club.

"People also connect me to that ... mostly think that's cuz they don't know me," Rogan said. "Because I look right-wing and I did kind of help Trump."

White goes on to laugh before Rogan pops in to say, "I've been left-wing my whole life."

Rogan described many of his views as "left-wing" but said he had been worried about government overreach.

"What we were sold with the Trump administration would be (overreach) would end, and there'd be a 'drain the swamp,'" Rogan said. "Obviously, it's not been ideal in that regard."

Rogan also said he would debate Hinchcliffe, who he classified as fully right-wing. Still, he echoed some commonly right-wing stances, calling "open borders," COVID mandates and vaccine requirements "insane."

Joe Rogan discusses abortion, women's rights

White said he voted for former President Joe Biden out of concerns for women's rights, which Rogan clarified he meant abortion access.

"The abortion rights thing is a weird one," Rogan said. "I don't think I have a right to tell anybody what to do with their body. I'm not a woman. I've never been pregnant."

He then goes on to express fear about abortions that happen later in pregnancy, which are exceedingly rare. Before the Dobbs decision overturned the right to an abortion, about 1% of abortions occurred after 21 weeks, according to KFF .

Rogan and White were discussing country star Jelly Roll's August appearance on "Jimmy Kimmel Live!" a late-night show that has long been at odds with the Trump administration. Jelly Roll was discussing his weight loss journey when he took some digs at Trump.

"Think about this, y'all. In the last few years, I've lost 300 pounds. That means I've lost an entire Donald Trump ," the 41-year-old singer said. "And let's be honest, based on his approval ratings , it seems like most of the country wants to do the same thing."

Rogan and White were discussing the singer's dip into comedy and the backlash against the monologue.

"Trump supporters are (expletive) nuts, man. They're rabid. He represents something other than just a person to them," Rogan said. "He represents ... a leader they wish they had."

Contributing: Taijuan Moorman, USA TODAY

Kinsey Crowley is the Trump Connect reporter for the USA TODAY Network. Reach her at KCrowley@usatodayco.com. Follow her on X (Twitter) , Threads , Bluesky and TikTok .

articles.title: Serie A | Monza 2-1 Sassuolo: Varela double to enjoy first win
articles.summary: Monza celebrated their first Serie A victory of the season thanks to a Gustavo Varela brace, as Sassuolo stumbled despite the late Vasilije Adzic free kick.I...
articles.body:
Monza celebrated their first Serie A victory of the season thanks to a Gustavo Varela brace, as Sassuolo stumbled despite the late Vasilije Adzic free kick.

Ivan Juric was feeling the pressure after just one point from four rounds, missing Patrick Ciurria , Jan Ziolkowski and Matteo Pessina , but recovering Ricardo Mangas from an ankle knock and giving Noel Tornqvist his debut on loan from Como . The Neroverdi had seven points from the last three games, including a 3-2 victory over Juventus , but Jay Idzes joined Cristian Volpato , Sebastian Walukiewicz , Daniel Boloca , Fali Candé and Ismael Koné on the treatment table.

MONZA, ITALY – SEPTEMBER 18: Domenico Berardi of Sassuolo in action during the Serie A match between AC Monza and US Sassuolo at U-Power Stadium on September 18, 2026 in Monza, Italy. (Photo by Claudio Villa/Getty Images)

The hosts had an aggressive start, a double ricochet preventing Jay Robinson from turning in the Patrick Cutrone assist during the opening minute.

Debutant Noel Tornqvist had to make a desperate save on Domenico Berardi from point-bank range, meeting the Armand Laurienté cross from the left.

Tornqvist also had to make the difficult save on Darryl Bakola from a tricky angle, then rushed off his line to deny Kristian Thorstvedt after an inspired Sebastiano Esposito back-heel flick. The goalkeeper, already sporting a protective helmet due to a previous injury, was glad of that after accidentally getting a shin in the forehead.

MONZA, ITALY – SEPTEMBER 18: Kristian Thorstvedt of Sassuolo and Noel Tornqvist of Monza in action during the Serie A match between AC Monza and US Sassuolo at U-Power Stadium on September 18, 2026 in Monza, Italy. (Photo by Claudio Villa/Getty Images)

Cutrone hesitated before finishing off a Gustavo Varela pass and was robbed when pulling the trigger, then after the restart saw his low drive fingertipped round the near post.

Monza scored on the resulting corner, as Arijanet Muric let the Varela header squirm through his fingers from six yards, a real howler from the Sassuolo goalkeeper who seemed to have the ball fully under control.

MONZA, ITALY – SEPTEMBER 18: Gustavo Varela of AC Monza scores his team's first goal during the Serie A match between AC Monza and US Sassuolo at U-Power Stadium on September 18, 2026 in Monza, Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images)

Sassuolo were undone by another corner, as Dany Mota Carvalho was brought down clumsily by Esposito for a penalty, converted by Varela to complete his brace.

Vasilije Adzic fired just over after good work from Josh Doig , but it was so nearly 3-0 when Samuele Birindelli 's angled drive flashed across the face of goal to skim the far post.

MONZA, ITALY – SEPTEMBER 18: Gustavo Varela of AC Monza scores his team's second goal from the penalty spot during the Serie A match between AC Monza and US Sassuolo at U-Power Stadium on September 18, 2026 in Monza, Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images)

Adzic scored the last-gasp winner against Juventus , and this time he curled a powerful right-footed free kick into the far top corner and gave Sassuolo hope late on. Once again, the goalkeeper seemed to be at fault, positioning the wall incorrectly and leaving himself unsighted.

Sassuolo were inches away from an equaliser in stoppages, as Kieron Bowie 's header from an Adzic cross bounced off the top of the far post with Tornqvist able only to watch and hope.

articles.title: Taylor Swift quiet as friend Ed Sheeran takes heat over Macklemore's 'Free Palestine' concert fiasco
articles.summary: Taylor Swift's silence on Ed Sheeran's Macklemore controversy raises questions as the fallout over "Free Palestine" chants continues to escalate.
articles.body: Taylor Swift hasn’t publicly spoken out in support of close friend Ed Sheeran as controversy over Macklemore's removal has engulfed Sheeran's latest tour. Sheeran has faced scrutiny from some pro-Palestinian and anti-Israel activists after his tour promoter and venues dropped rapper Macklemore from his Loop Tour after Macklemore’s onstage chants of "Free Palestine" earlier this month. Groups, including StopAntisemitism and the Combat Antisemitism Movement called for Macklemore's removal, while singer Pink criticized Macklemore's performance. MACKLEMORE DOUBLES DOWN AFTER GETTING KICKED OFF ED SHEERAN TOUR AFTER PRO-PALESTINE STANCE It was during his opening set on the tour at New Jersey’s MetLife Stadium when the Grammy-winning Macklemore also described Israel’s actions using terms such as "genocide" and "apartheid." Since the dust-up, Sheeran released a statement addressing the situation, saying the decision to remove Macklemore was made by the tour’s promoters and venues, not by him personally. He also noted his desire to continue the tour and not let down fans or crew members who rely on his concerts for their income. That was followed by four of his tour openers withdrawing from his concerts in solidarity with Macklemore, while also noting their own opposition to what they described as genocide in Gaza. Macklemore notably drew fierce criticism in 2014 when he donned what appeared to be an antisemitic costume caricaturing Jewish people, although he claimed it was unintentional. As Sheeran has been navigating one of the most public controversies of his career, his longtime friend and collaborator Swift has been quiet, reflective of a career where she's generally, but not always, stayed out of political strife. ED SHEERAN FACES GROWING BACKLASH AS RADIO STATION BANS SONGS, PROTEST GROUPS RESPOND TO MACKLEMORE'S REMOVAL Swift has shared a close personal and professional relationship with Sheeran spanning more than a decade. It has even been described as one of the most high-profile friendships in modern music history, with the pair mutually supporting each other through the years and collaborating both in the studio and onstage. Sheeran appeared as the opening act for the North American leg of Swift’s "Red Tour" in 2013, and the two have teamed up on songs including the duet "Everything Has Changed" from that tour and the 2021 song "Run." He also was a "surprise guest" during her Eras Tour. Plenty of other memorable moments have ensued between the two. When Swift won her first BRIT Award in 2015, she publicly thanked Sheeran in her acceptance speech, crediting him with teaching her about British culture and pubs. Sheeran has been known to appear at her concerts, one time dressed as a clown as he went onto the stage during one of her Nashville shows. Both artists have often described how they’re able to relate to one another because of the unique pressures they experience at their level of fame. Swift’s reps are known for protecting the singer’s brand, and Swift has historically been selective about when she speaks out, but she has used her platform to advocate for some progressive causes in recent years, such as endorsing Kamala Harris and supporting gay rights. She also has tried to get more voters registered, including when she endorsed Harris in 2024. CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE In 2018, Swift criticized Republican Tennessee Senate candidate Marsha Blackburn over her conservative voting record and opposition to LGBTQ+ and women’s rights, instead endorsing her Democratic opponent, former Tennessee Gov. Phil Bredesen. She also described President Donald Trump as a poor leader during the COVID-19 pandemic and accused him of cheating to win. Some who've worked in the entertainment industry think it's best for performers to remain quiet about politics, whether it's Macklemore, Swift or any other celebrity. "My general feeling is they ought to stay in their own lane," David Sams, CEO of Sam’s Global Companies, a conglomerate of media networks and talent management, and former head of global marketing and creative affairs at King World, told Fox News Digital. "It’s a lot of noise, and with everything going on in the world right now, to even give five seconds to their shenanigans is ridiculous." Swift has also at times been criticized by the left for being insufficiently outspoken on issues. articles.title: Belmont Park reopens as new sports and entertainment destination
articles.summary: ELMONT, N.Y. (PIX11) — The horses are running again at Belmont Park. For the first time in three years, race calls echo across the iconic Nassau County track...
articles.body:
ELMONT, N.Y. (PIX11) — The horses are running again at Belmont Park .

For the first time in three years, race calls echo across the iconic Nassau County track as thousands of fans gather for the reopening of a completely redesigned Belmont Park complex.

The familiar sounds returned as the trumpet signaled the first call to post since 2023 and horses took to one of four newly constructed tracks, including a synthetic racing surface designed to support a longer racing season.

Visitors said Belmont's appeal is also about the atmosphere.

"The events are about showmanship and fashion and excitement, beauty and coming together," said Stephanie Saltzman.

The new 5-story grandstand features luxury suites, expanded food and entertainment options, and additional green space. State and racing officials hope the venue will become a year-round sports and entertainment destination.

"It'll be good to hear that pitter-patter and the trot going around again. It'll be exciting," said Bob Barker, president of the Locustwood-Gotham Civic Association.

Barker said he is also excited about the economic benefits the project could bring to the area.

The State of New York loaned the New York Racing Association $455 million to help finance construction of the new facility. The funding will be repaid with interest under a long-term payment plan. The new complex cost about $550 million.

NYRA Chairman Marc Holliday said the investment extends beyond horse racing.

"Horse racing isn't just a sport. It's an economic engine. It's a connection to the agricultural roots," Holliday said.

Officials say the venue will host events throughout the year, including concerts, festivals and community gatherings.

"We set out to build a place that could be a concert and entertainment venue. It belongs not only to racing fans, but the community," New York Governor Kathy Hochul said.

Architect Meg McWilliam said designers focused on modernizing the facility while preserving the traditions that have long defined Belmont Park.

"What we focused on was bringing the venue into the 21st century and looking ahead while understanding the things that have been important to the Belmont experience," McWilliam said.

One of the most notable changes is the expanded paddock area, where fans can watch horses and jockeys prepare before races.

NYRA Vice President of Communications Pat McKenna said the redesigned space is intended to bring visitors closer to the action.

"Friends, families, young people can get up close and interact with the crowd. It's a focal point," McKenna said.

In June 2027, the Belmont Stakes will return to Belmont Park. For the past three championships, it was hosted upstate in Saratoga, another iconic venue.

articles.standfirst: Dupla paralisou a apresentação diante de uma plateia recorde no Jaguariúna Rodeo Festival para abrir espaço para a passagem da equipe de atendimento.
articles.summary: Dupla paralisou a apresentação diante de uma plateia recorde no Jaguariúna Rodeo Festival para abrir espaço para a passagem da equipe de atendimento.
articles.body:
Zezé Di Camargo e Luciano interromperam o show que abriu a edição 2026 do Jaguariúna Rodeo Festival, na noite desta sexta-feira (18), para auxiliar no atendimento a uma pessoa que passou mal na plateia .

Ao perceber a movimentação do público, os sertanejos pararam a apresentação e pediram a colaboração dos fãs para a passagem da equipe de socorro.

"Abre aqui só pra ter segurança", pediu Luciano. Em seguida, Zezé reforçou: "Abre um caminhozinho para a segurança passar e atender a pessoa".

Durante a pausa, os artistas acompanharam a situação e buscaram informações junto à equipe responsável pelo atendimento.

"Tudo bem, pessoal? O bombeiro está pedindo para abrir aqui o caminho. Só abrir aqui para o pessoal passar com a pessoa", disse Zezé ao público.

O g1 apurou que a pessoa foi socorrida e encaminhada a um posto médico na arena.

Até a última atualização desta reportagem, não haviam sido divulgadas informações sobre identidade, idade, sexo ou estado de saúde do atendido.

"Você ouviu o Medina dando uma entrevista, falando que está pensando em colocar a música setaneja lá no Rock in Rio. Mas Barretos, aqui, Jaguariúna, Americana, tudo já ultrapassou o Rock in Rio há muito tempo", afirmou.

Zezé tocou no assunto ao falar justamente da força da música sertaneja, que há décadas ganhou reconhecimento popular.

"Quem nunca andou dentro de um coletivo lotado com um radinho de pilha me ouvindo, ouvindo uma música sertaneja numa rádio? Eu já fiz isso demais. Não era reconhecido naquela época. Então, hoje aconteceu, hoje é a música número um do Brasil", disse.

articles.title: Mariana Fagundes prepara ônibus para chegada da filha e planeja levar Isis para a estrada: 'Já vai nascer no palco' | G1
articles.standfirst: Às vésperas de sua estreia no Jaguariúna Rodeo Festival, cantora, grávida da primeira filha, afirma que a bebê vai acompanhá-la em hotéis, viagens e bastidores de shows pelo Brasil.
articles.summary: Às vésperas de sua estreia no Jaguariúna Rodeo Festival, cantora, grávida da primeira filha, afirma que a bebê vai acompanhá-la em hotéis, viagens e bastidores de shows pelo Brasil
articles.body:
Mariana Fagundes chega ao Jaguariúna Rodeo Festival para sua estreia no evento, marcada para a próxima sexta-feira (25), em meio a um momento especial da vida pessoal. Grávida de Isis , sua primeira filha, a cantora do hit "Peão Todo Tatuado" afirma que pretende conciliar a maternidade com a agenda de shows e já prepara a bebê para a rotina na estrada .

Segundo a artista, a ideia é que Isis acompanhe de perto a rotina da mãe pelo Brasil.

"A Isis já vai nascer praticamente no palco."

Mariana conta que os preparativos envolvem até mesmo a estrutura utilizada durante as viagens pelo país. "A gente tá preparando o mundinho dela na estrada, a gente tá preparando o ônibus para a chegada dela", disse.

A cantora afirma que pretende manter a filha próxima da rotina de apresentações, acompanhando os bastidores e os deslocamentos da equipe.

"Com certeza ela vai acompanhar todos os bastidores, eu vou levar ela para os hotéis, se Deus permitir, eu vou amamentar ela nos hotéis, no ônibus, e a bichinha já vai pro trecho comigo", avisou.

Mariana Fagundes anunciando que está grávida. — Foto: Rede social.

A maternidade chega em um dos momentos mais importantes da carreira da sertaneja.

Embalada pelo sucesso de "Peão Todo Tatuado", Mariana também se prepara para subir pela primeira vez ao palco do Jaguariúna Rodeo Festival, uma apresentação que ela define como a realização de um sonho.

"Tô superanimada com o show Jaguariúna, não vejo a hora, é um sonho realizado. Eu já estive ali como plateia em outros shows, então, meu Deus, imagina, essa cantora aqui tá superansiosa. Eu tô agradecida a Deus, não vejo a hora de chegar o momento de subir naquele palcão gigante, enorme e mostrar que eu mereci ter essa oportunidade de estar naquele palco lindão", disse.

Para a apresentação, a cantora promete um repertório marcado pela animação e pela proximidade com os fãs. "A gente vai fazer um showzão, um show família, alegre, contagiante".

Estreante em Jaguariúna, Mariana Fagundes, dona do hit "Peão todo tatuado", soma 12,1 milhões de ouvites mensais em plataforma de streaming — Foto: Érico Andrade/g1

Em meio à agenda de shows, Mariana também prepara um novo projeto audiovisual. A artista revelou que vai gravar um DVD em outubro, embora ainda mantenha em sigilo as músicas que farão parte do trabalho.

"Em outubro, vamos gravar um DVD lindão, um DVD maravilhoso. Eu não posso ainda cantar as músicas para vocês, mas peço para todo mundo acompanhar aí", disse.

Segundo a cantora, o repertório está sendo construído com o apoio de compositores consagrados.

"O repertório tá sendo criado com muito carinho. Muitos compositores incríveis, compositores de sucesso. Estão todos me apoiando, me ajudando pra gente arrebentar nesse repertório."

Estreante em Jaguariúna, Mariana Fagundes, dona do hit "Peão todo tatuado", revela a gravação de um DVD em outubro — Foto: Reprodução

Questionada sobre os sonhos que ainda pretende realizar na carreira, Mariana citou alguns dos nomes mais importantes do sertanejo entre as parcerias que gostaria de concretizar.

"Profissionalmente eu tenho vários feats aí que eu sonho. Simone Mendes, a própria Ana Castela, Maiara & Maraisa. Essa mulherada maravilhosa, eu tenho um sonho de gravar com elas."

A lista inclui ainda artistas que ajudaram a construir a história do gênero.

"Chitãozinho & Xororó, que eu amo. Zezé. Ai, meu Deus, tem tanta gente. Eu quero fazer tantos feats ainda. Deus me dê muita saúde pra eu realizar os nossos sonhos", completou.

articles.title: Como a fama de bom moço da música contribuiu para a maior crise da carreira de Ed Sheeran | G1
articles.standfirst: Ed Sheeran tenta se afastar de política e controvérsias, mas seu posicionamento gerou críticas e até uma crise na sua turnê de 2026.
articles.summary: Ed Sheeran tenta se afastar de política e controvérsias, mas seu posicionamento gerou críticas e até uma crise na sua turnê de 2026.
articles.body:
Como a fama de bom moço da música contribuiu para a maior crise da carreira de Ed Sheeran — Foto: (Sarah Jeynes/BBC)

O cantor britânico Ed Sheeran enfrenta o momento mais controverso da sua carreira.

Sheeran é um dos compositores mais bem sucedidos de todos os tempos. Ele já vendeu mais de 120 milhões de discos e passou mais de 1 mil semanas nas paradas de sucesso dos Estados Unidos.

Parte do seu apelo, além das suas canções insidiosamente cativantes, vem da sua personalidade simples. Ele parece ser um fã e se veste como eles ao voltar de trem de Glastonbury, na Inglaterra, mesmo sendo um dos principais destaques do festival.

Sheeran cultivou cuidadosamente uma imagem pública inofensiva e receptiva a todos.

Em 2014, ele doou todo o seu guarda-roupa para lojas de caridade. E, naquele mesmo ano, ele adotou um gato de um mês de idade, que foi salvo da eutanásia e recebeu o nome de Graham.

Atualmente, ele administra uma organização beneficente que oferece aulas de música para menores de 18 anos, na sua casa de campo em Suffolk, na Inglaterra.

Sheeran tenta ficar afastado da política. Normalmente, ele só se envolve para defender questões como proteção de direitos autorais e revenda de ingressos, ou para levantar questões sobre o impacto do Brexit sobre as turnês de músicos.

Mas sua tendência é de esquerda. Nas eleições gerais britânicas de 2017, ele afirmou ter apoiado o então líder trabalhista Jeremy Corbyn, embora não tenha participado da campanha.

"As pessoas achavam que, como eu não aparecia ao lado dele, não era apoiador de Corbyn", contou Sheeran ao jornal britânico Sunday Times.

"Se você me conhecesse como pessoa e ouvisse minhas músicas, poderia ter um palpite bem fundamentado de que ele seria o tipo de pessoa que eu realmente apoiaria."

Em relação a questões fora do mundo musical, Sheeran prefere permanecer recolhido.

Seu raciocínio, segundo ele próprio, é que a música deve unir as pessoas. Ele considera seus shows como "locais de segurança e refúgio", construídos com base na humanidade comum.

Mas, nesta semana, este argumento desmoronou, criando uma crise para sua reputação e sua carreira.

Cantor enfrenta polêmica — Foto: Shaun Whitmore/BBC

Provavelmente, você já sabe da história.

Macklemore foi escolhido para abrir a turnê de Sheeran nos Estados Unidos. E, na primeira noite, ele fez um discurso dizendo "Palestina livre" e mostrando imagens da destruição na Faixa de Gaza.

Na noite seguinte, ele se referiu ao número de mortos como genocídio, uma acusação rejeitada por Israel. E enfrentou as críticas que se seguiram.

A organização StopAntisemitism acusou Macklemore de criar uma "armadilha" para o público. E os donos de estádios, aparentemente liderados pelo bilionário dono do time de futebol americano New England Patriots, Robert Kraft, pressionaram Sheeran e seus promotores a retirá-lo da turnê.

Depois de uma semana de discussões nos bastidores, eles conseguiram.

Na terça-feira (15/9), Sheeran publicou uma declaração, afirmando que os promotores tomaram a decisão, não ele.

Ele afirmou ter tentado construir pontes entre as partes, sem sucesso. E que ele "não foi conivente", defendendo que sua decisão de permanecer fora do debate sobre o Oriente Médio em público não era prova de que ele "não se importava".

"Estou indignado com o conflito entre Israel e a Palestina", escreveu ele. "O sofrimento e a dor causada nos dois lados é uma tragédia humana."

"Existem guerras demais em todo o mundo, causando dores imensuráveis, e nenhuma delas deveria ser tolerada."

"Existe uma razão por que não uso minha plataforma profissional para a política", prosseguiu ele. "Meu público inclui jovens e muitas crianças, de todas as origens."

Ed Sheeran se apresentou com Macklemore no Festival de Música iHeartRadio de 2014 em Las Vegas, nos Estados Unidos — Foto: Getty Images/Via BBC

Se Sheeran está tão preocupado com as crianças, os críticos questionam por que ele não mencionou as milhares de crianças mortas na Faixa de Gaza.

Outros relembram que sua abstenção da política não foi absoluta.

Em 2018, ele vestiu uma camiseta com os dizeres "Justiça para Grenfell" no Estádio de Wembley, em Londres. Era uma referência ao incêndio da Grenfell Tower, na capital britânica, ocorrido no ano anterior.

Sheeran também participou do Festival pela Ucrânia em 2022 e gravou com a banda U2 uma canção de protesto sobre a guerra naquele país em 2026.

Foram também levantadas questões sobre sua relação com Kraft. Sheeran cantou no seu casamento em 2022 e, em uma entrevista após o evento, o chamou de "superdoce".

O jornalista especializado em música Jeffrey Ingold declarou que a aparente aceitação da decisão de retirar Macklemore da turnê pareceu "covardia" da parte de Sheeran.

"Ele é um dos maiores músicos do mundo", destacou Ingold à BBC Rádio 5 Live.

"Ele tem poder e influência. E, basicamente, ele lavou as mãos e disse 'não é responsabilidade minha'."

"Ele tinha alternativas, certo?", prosseguiu o jornalista.

"Ele poderia ter dito aos promotores e aos donos dos espaços, incluindo Robert Kraft: 'Quer saber? Não vamos fazer os shows ali. Se você não permitir que todos nós nos apresentemos, não vamos fazer.' Ele poderia ter encontrado locais alternativos."

A turnê de Sheeran entrou em crise horas depois da sua declaração.

Outros três artistas que participariam da turnê — Finneas, Aaron Rowe e Lukas Graham — anunciaram sua saída, expressando apoio a Macklemore.

A banda irlandesa Beoga também desistiu. Ela serve de apoio a Sheeran para músicas como Galway Girl e Nancy Mulligan . E Finneas estava escalado para abrir os shows de Sheeran em São Paulo, no início de dezembro.

Vários deles afirmaram que a decisão de excluir Macklemore, tomada por um grupo de bilionários donos de locais de shows, representava supressão da liberdade de expressão.

Outras personalidades do setor musical e de fora dele também se manifestaram.

A estrela do pop Pink, que pertence à comunidade judaica, compartilhou um meme contra Macklemore acompanhado da sua própria mensagem, explicando por que ela desaprova os comentários do rapper.

De uma hora para outra e contra sua vontade, Sheeran passou a ser o centro de uma tempestade política em torno de uma das questões mais polêmicas que existem.

Será que Ed Sheeran poderia ter lidado melhor com a controvérsia quando ela surgiu? Certamente que sim.

Na sua declaração, ele afirmou que gostaria de prosseguir com a turnê, para não decepcionar os fãs e a equipe que depende dos seus shows para ganhar a vida.

Se ele tivesse ameaçado desistir das apresentações, poderia ter enquadrado a questão como um protesto em favor da liberdade de expressão. Mas ele ainda teria sido inevitavelmente interpretado como endossando as declarações de Macklemore.

Por isso, Sheeran ficou preso em um beco sem saída. Ele estava condenado, qualquer que fosse a sua decisão.

Sua imagem de bom moço sofreu um enorme abalo. E o tom da sua declaração ("não é minha responsabilidade") certamente não ajudou a reduzir a crise.

"Acho que isso irá mudar a forma como as pessoas olharão para ele a partir de agora", afirma Ingold.

"Ele disse que não é conivente, mas, na verdade, ele é totalmente conivente com o que está acontecendo."

O editor-executivo de música da revista Variety, Jem Aswad, afirma que o episódio mostra que "não se pode ser neutro nesta questão".

Mas ele destaca que a maioria das pessoas não vai aos shows de Sheeran para serem relembradas sobre questões como a Faixa de Gaza. "Eles vão para deixar de pensar nisso e se divertir."

Aswad duvida que esta controvérsia cause grandes danos à carreira do cantor. Ele não acredita que a maior parte das críticas "venha necessariamente dos fãs de Ed Sheeran ".

"Elas vêm de pessoas que questionam a forma como ele se comportou nesta situação e não acho que muitas dessas pessoas realmente sejam fãs de Ed Sheeran ", destaca ele.

Teremos a prova quando Sheeran se apresentar no seu próximo show na Filadélfia, neste sábado (19/9). Uma parcela do público poderá expressar suas ideias, mas muitos estarão ali apenas para apreciar a música.

A perda da sua banda de apoio também não é o desastre que pode parecer. Em turnês anteriores, Sheeran foi o único artista no palco, acompanhado por um pedal de loop, sem depender de outros músicos.

Mas, quando esta rodada de shows terminar em dezembro, no México, seus próximos passos precisarão ser cuidadosamente planejados.

Nesta era de descontentamento febril, permanecer fora dos confrontos talvez seja simplesmente impossível.

articles.title: Ajulliacosta é indicada ao Grammy Latino por Novo Testamento | G1
articles.standfirst: Artista concorre na categoria Melhor Álbum de Música Urbana em Língua Portuguesa; "Novo Testamento" alcançou 1 milhão de reproduções nas plataformas digitais em apenas 72 horas após o lançamento.
articles.summary: Ajulliacosta disputa o Grammy Latino de Melhor Álbum de Música Urbana com "Novo Testamento", sucesso que atingiu 1 milhão de plays em 72 horas.
articles.body:
🎤🎶 “O que a Julia quer? O que a Julia vai ser? Muda a vida, muda tudo, mas não muda a minha sede” , diz um trecho de uma das músicas do álbum “Novo Testamento”, da rapper mogiana Ajulliacosta.

Se, na letra, a artista pergunta o que a Julia vai ser, agora já existe ao menos uma resposta: indicada ao Grammy Latino na categoria Melhor Álbum de Música Urbana em Língua Portuguesa . Ajulliacosta sempre acreditou no potencial do projeto, mas não imaginava até onde ele poderia levá-la.

“‘O Novo Testamento’ era um projeto que eu coloquei muita energia, então eu imaginava que ele daria muito bom. Mas isso eu acho que é a coisa mais legal de não saber de tudo, né? Porque eu imaginava que ele seria bom, mas não imaginava quais coisas ele me traria, então estou muito grata”, disse em entrevista ao g1.

Ajulliacosta concorre ao Grammy Latino com o álbum “Novo Testamento” — Foto: Michelle Gomes/Divulgação

Ajulliacosta concorre na categoria ao lado de nomes conhecidos do rap brasileiro, como Emicida, Budah e Don L.

“As expectativas [para o Grammy Latino] são vivenciar isso, sabe? Poder aproveitar desse momento também, porque é um momento muito especial tanto para mim, como fã de música, quanto profissional”, ressaltou.

📲🎧 Ajulliacosta tem atualmente cerca de 1,7 milhão de ouvintes mensais em uma plataforma digital. Nas redes sociais, são mais de 1 milhão de seguidores. Antes de alcançar esse público, porém, a artista viveu dos 7 aos 15 anos em um conjunto habitacional da Companhia de Desenvolvimento Habitacional e Urbano (CDHU), em Mogi das Cruzes. Na época, ela já fazia planos para o futuro.

“Eu sempre fui uma menina com muitos sonhos, mas o Grammy, apesar de sempre projetar uma boa carreira artística, o Grammy, ele me pegou de surpresa. Essa indicação me pegou muito de surpresa. É uma coisa que a gente sempre deseja, mas a gente não fica esperando tanto, né? Então eu sou muito grata e eu diria pra ela [a menina que morava em Mogi] continuar sonhando, porque vale a pena”.

A rapper acredita que a indicação também pode ser inspiração para outras meninas.

“Eu acho que dá ainda mais incentivo, assim, sabe? Quando veio pra mim a indicação, eu pensei muito nos meus processos, escrevendo no meu quarto. Então, eu acho que incentiva outras meninas, faz a gente conseguir sonhar mais longe”, finalizou.

“Novo Testamento” tem 11 faixas e foi lançado em 16 de setembro de 2025 e alcançou 1 milhão de reproduções nas plataformas digitais em apenas 72 horas. Os shows de lançamento em São Paulo tiveram os ingressos esgotados.

Atualmente, Ajulliacosta está em turnê pela Europa, com apresentações marcadas em Portugal, Espanha e Alemanha.

articles.body:
O apresentador Fred Bruno marcou presença na primeira noite do Jaguariúna Rodeo Festival 2026. Cheio de estilo, o titular do Globo Esporte em São Paulo disse que o look escolhido foi "baratíssimo".

"Meu outfit? Baratíssimo. Sei lá, acho que não passa de R$ 700", respondeu, aos risos.

Segundo Fred, a peça de destaque do visual foi uma jaqueta com estampa animal print que ele comprou já pensando em uma ocasião ligada ao universo sertanejo.

"Vi essa jaqueta aqui na loja e falei: 'Pô, em algum rodeio, alguma festa sertaneja eu vou usar'. É meio animal print", contou.

O apresentador afirmou que não segue fórmulas quando o assunto é moda e defendeu que cada pessoa use aquilo com que se sente confortável.

"Eu sou sempre a favor daqueles que vestem o que têm vontade", afirmou.

Entre as peças que mais gosta de incorporar ao visual, Fred destacou os chapéus, acessório tradicional dos rodeios e festas sertanejas. "Gosto muito de usar chapéu", disse.

articles.summary: The trailer of 'Dhoomakethu' has been released and it promises a Malayalam film that is built around time travel, comedy, mystery and murder. Directed.
articles.body: The trailer of 'Dhoomakethu' has been released and it promises a Malayalam film that is built around time travel, comedy, mystery and murder. Directed by Sudhi Maddison, the movie features Sajin Gopu and Nikhila Vimal in the lead roles. The film is scheduled to hit theaters on September 25.The trailer presents a curious situation involving a newly married couple. It also hints at a repeating cycle that leaves Sajin Gopu's character searching for answers.'Dhoomakethu' trailer introduces a strange time loopThe trailer begins with Sajin Gopu's character discussing an unusual situation with his friend played by Ganapathi. The mystery starts after he marries Nikhila Vimal's character.Their first night together soon takes an unexpected turn. A mysterious killer enters the picture. This leads to a deadly sequence of events. The situation has similarities to the concept used in 'Happy Death Day'.After the incident, the day appears to reset. Sajin Gopu's character is forced to return to the same point in time. He then finds himself caught in a cycle that he cannot seem to escape. The trailer does not reveal the identity of the killer. It also leaves open the possibility that more than one person could be involved in the mystery. Shine Tom Chacko's character also adds to the mystery.Sajin Gopu searches for the killerThe repeating timeline creates the main conflict for Sajin Gopu's character. He appears determined to understand why the same events keep happening. His attempts to spend his first night with his wife are repeatedly interrupted by the strange events, create a fun vibe.The protagonist's investigation gradually becomes a mission to identify the person behind the killings. Every reset seems to offer another clue. It also appears to bring new problems for him.'Dhoomakethu' explores the time-loop conceptThe film appears to draw from the broader time-loop genre seen in movies such as 'Groundhog Day' and 'Happy Death Day'. However, the story seems to place the concept within a distinctly Malayalam setting.The makers describe 'Dhoomakethu' as a grounded take on the time-loop idea. The trailer also keeps the larger plot concealed. It does not explain why the protagonist is trapped in the cycle. The reason behind the killings remains another major mystery.Sajin Gopu and Nikhila Vimal lead the castSajin Gopu and Nikhila Vimal headline the film. Shine Tom Chacko, Ganapathi and Siddharth Bharathan also play key roles. Sudhi Maddison, who previously directed 'Neymar' and 'Sookshmadarshini', has helmed the project. Sonny and Manu have penned the screenplay.The first-look poster had earlier created interest among moviegoers. It featured underwater visuals, which are relatively uncommon in Malayalam cinema.Jinto George is the cinematographer, while Vivek Harshan handles the editing. articles.title: Rob Reiner murder case: Son Nick Reiner unable to access money from trust fund for 'jail commissary'
articles.summary: Nick Reiner, son of Rob Reiner, struggles to access his trust fund amidst allegations of murdering his parents. Learn about the ongoing legal battles and trust fund complications involving $1.6 million.
articles.body: TRIGGER WARNING: This article contains gruesome details of murder and violence, which could be triggering for some readers.Rob Reiner and Michele Singer's son, Nick Reiner, recently made a statement while awaiting his next trial date. The 33-year-old has been in jail since December last year for allegedly stabbing his parents to death. Since then, multiple reports have shared that Reiner has attempted to access the trust fund that Rob set up; however, he has been unable to access the money because of the ongoing case. In a new update, filings revealed that he still has not received any monetary help from the trust fund.Here’s what we know so far about the case.Nick Reiner has not received money from trust fundSince his time in custody since last year, there have been multiple reports of Reiner filing for an appeal to access the trust fund for legal fees. PEOPLE reported that since then, Nick has not been able to get access to any of the money. Awaiting trial for the death of his parents, Nick has not received “even USD 5 for the jail commissary."The Nick Reiner Children’s Trust, which was established on December 2, 1993. The successor trustee Jodi Pais Montgomery and former trustee Paul R Kanin have filed objections to his continuous requests to access the trust fund which is reportedly worth USD 1.6 million.In the new filing on September 17, Reiner’s attorney stated that he has not been able to get access to basic amenities in jail or to even hire private defence counsel. They wrote in the filing, “In the meantime, Nick still has not been able to access even USD 5 from his trust to buy basic subsistence items from the jail commissary.”They further shared in the filing, “Since then, Nick has been unable to access money that is lawfully his own—to re-engage criminal defense counsel, or even for basic subsistence items from the jail commissary.” They also stated in the documents that the maturity date for the trust fund was based on when he turned 30, after which, around USD 558,000, came under his name. They further argued that “The Slayer Statute, the sole remaining basis for withholding this money, takes away what a person receives as a result of someone’s death. It does not implicate money that became Nick’s years earlier.”They also alleged in a second filing that was done on the same day to reply to Kanin’s objections that they had been promised access to the funds from the trust and that some amount would be transferred to Nick’s commissary account. The filmmaker began by remembering actor Vijay and the support he received from him at an important stage in his career. From Vijay’s continued encouragement to his role in Atlee taking up 'Jawan,' the director recalled several personal moments. He also spoke about young composer Sai Abhyankkar, Vijay Sethupathi’s role in bringing 'Baththa' to him, and why he believes the film can connect with audiences across generations.Atlee credits Vijay for giving his career a major boostAtlee said that while 'Raja Rani' gave him recognition, his back-to-back films with Vijay transformed his career. “I might have bought this shirt, this pair of trousers, and this watch with my hard work. But if it wasn’t for my brother, my Thalapathy, I wouldn’t have got the chance. I became known after 'Raja Rani,' but that man gave me a life, back to back, back to back,” he said. Recalling how Vijay encouraged him when Shah Rukh Khan approached him for 'Jawan,' Atlee added, “When Shah Rukh sir came to my office, Vijay anna told me, ‘I don’t know what you are going to do, but please make that film. Your life will change.’ And my life changed.” Atlee also said he was not praising Vijay in the hope of getting another opportunity, pointing out that Vijay has now become the Tamil Nadu Chief Minister.Atlee says Vijay is creating a new generation of political awarenessAtlee also spoke about the change he believes Vijay’s political entry has created among younger people. “The next generation will be strong in politics. The only reason is Vijay anna. I am not speaking about politics. In my generation, I never saw the Assembly. But now, a five-year-old is watching the Assembly in the morning. articles.title: 'I didn't know if people will like this film or not': 'Gondhal' director Santosh Davakhar on Oscars entry
articles.summary: Marathi filmmaker Santosh Davakhar has opened up about his vision behind 'Gondhal', which has been selected as India's official entry for the Oscars. .
articles.body: Marathi filmmaker Santosh Davakhar has opened up about his vision behind 'Gondhal', which has been selected as India's official entry for the Oscars. The director said in a recent interview that he wanted the film to showcase India's cultural identity to audiences beyond the country.Santosh Davakhar said his focus was to present Indian culture and heritage through a cinematic narrative. He also revealed that his experiences at international film festivals shaped his approach to the project.In a conversation with IANS, the filmmaker recalled being unsure about the response to 'Gondhal'. However, he had a clear goal while developing the Marathi thriller. "To be honest, I didn't know if people will like this film or not. My first priority was that I have to make this film internationally," he said.Santosh Davakhar on India's image through cinemaThe filmmaker said his experiences at Cannes and other international festivals made him think about the way Indian cinema is viewed globally.During his festival visits, Santosh Davakhar observed that conversations around Indian films often focused on subjects such as poverty and casteism. He said these remain important issues but felt India's cultural heritage also deserved wider representation. "When I was in Cannes and other festivals internationally, that time I got to know about the representation of Indian films, and how people think that the films here are about poverty and casteism," he said.Santosh Davakhar said he wanted 'Gondhal' to present another aspect of the country. His intention was to bring Indian traditions and cultural richness into the storytelling."This is an important issue in India. But apart from that, India has a rich heritage, a proud culture. And I wanted to represent that culture in a cinematic way," Davakhar said.'Gondhal' director drew from international cinemaHis exposure to world cinema also became an important part of the filmmaking process. Santosh Davakhar recalled watching several movies during his time at Cannes. The filmmaker said he watched three to four films every day during the festival. He eventually watched more than 40 films over 15 days."When I was in Cannes, I used to watch three-four films a day. In 15 days, I have watched more than 40 films. So that page automatically develops. And if you want to make an international film, your making should also be according to that," he said. He said watching international films helped him develop a better understanding of filmmaking and storytelling.Santosh Davakhar focuses on thriller and mysteryThe director also revealed that significant research went into developing the screenplay. He wanted to create a mystery thriller that audiences could follow without making the narrative overly complicated."I have done a lot of research on that. I have also done a lot of research on screenplay. And I have given people a thriller mystery in a very simple way. And along with that, I have also given a richness of rituals," he said.The film combines its mystery-driven storyline with rituals and elements of Indian culture. This forms a key part of Santosh Davakhar's approach to the project.'Gondhal' selected as India's official Oscar entry'Gondhal' has gained significant attention after being chosen as India's official entry for the Oscars. The Marathi film brings together thriller and mystery elements with traditional Indian rituals.'Gondhal' features Kishor Kadam in a prominent role. Ishita Deshmukh, Yogesh Sohoni, Nishad Bhoir, Anuj Prabhu, Suresh Vishwakarma and Vitthal Kale are also part of the cast.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Bristol singer on a mission to help people through music
articles.summary: Lady Nade, from Bristol, has performed at hospitals, prisons, care homes and schools.
articles.body:
A singer who used music to cope with childhood grief said she has made it her mission in life to help other people's wellbeing with the medium.

Lady Nade, from Bristol, turned to singing and songwriting at the age of 10 after her grandmother passed away. As a teenager, she embarked on a career in the field through free music workshops.

Now working as a music facilitator, she said her work had allowed her to build "incredible connections" with schoolchildren, prisoners, hospital patients, hospice patients and bereaved families.

"I have this sort of vision and mission that music should be accessible to all. I want to be part of that advocacy because music empowers people," Lady Nade said.

AI not a threat to films, say Shaun the Sheep creators

The Bristolian, who has released three albums since 2016, credited her grandparents for encouraging her to sing and perform as a child.

When her grandmother passed away, Lady Nade wrote letters and poems to her in an attempt to process her grief.

Her grandfather introduced her to a range of music through his collection of 1950s and 1960s rock 'n' roll, folk and Americana records, which helped her to develop her own taste and work.

"Me and my grandad would bond over listening to different mixtapes... it was part of my healing and grieving and I'd sing along at the top of my lungs and it'd remind me of these memories of my nan," she said.

During her teenage years, Lady Nade attended free music workshops at Bristol Beacon where she learned to sing and write songs with the help of mentors.

Through the scheme, she became a mentor herself and started working in the community as a Live Music Now facilitator.

The charity aims to create inclusive social impact and opportunity through music.

Lady Nade said: "Prisons, hospitals and care homes are inaccessible when it comes to music and art.

"Being able to actually outreach and be mobile and take music and turn it into a therapy and a process is so, so important.

"It helps people with their mental health and wellbeing. Music helps with senses, it helps the nervous system, it helps with anxiety, it helps with mood and it can help with memory."

The NHS recognises music as a form of therapy and employs specialised healthcare professionals to deliver sessions to people with a variety of needs.

Music has been linked to a wide range of health benefits - including lower blood pressure, improved heart rate and the release of endorphins .

Clare Maddocks, from the British Association for Music Therapy, works as a health and care professions council-registered music therapist who specialises in neurology.

She said the therapy method was suitable for everyone and no musical experience or skill was needed in order to benefit.

"We have a strong link between our emotions, our memory and music.

"Anytime we engage with music, we elicit a multimodal response in the brain.

"That means that music automatically taps into cognitive processes such as mood regulating parts of the brain and it also really helps to awaken the brain... then we can use that to help with our mood.

"You can start listening to a song and you can be feeling one way at the start of the song, but by the end of it, you might notice there's a bit of a shift happening in you," she said.

Lady Nade has performed in hospitals - including Southmead and Bristol Royal Infirmary - for patients suffering from neurological, mental and physical conditions, as well as in palliative care settings.

She said she previously performed for a palliative care patient - who used to play the trumpet - who sang along with her before he "peacefully passed away" later that day.

The bereaved family described her session as "a gift" that helped them to cope with "the worst time of their lives".

Lady Nade said sharing, performing and releasing her music - which often explores themes of identity, love and loss - felt like "a calling" for her.

"I realised through my work and through grief that shared grief validates other people's experiences.

"Grief can be validated when it's shared, but when we keep it in to ourselves, it can't be validated."

articles.title: Motivational quote of the day by Will Smith: ‘Fear is not real. It is a product of thoughts you create…fear is a choice,' the ‘After Earth’ star’s vision on reclaiming control over your emotional state
articles.summary: Will Smith has spent decades in the entertainment industry, rising from a middle-class upbringing in Philadelphia to becoming one of Hollywood’s most .
articles.body: Will Smith has spent decades in the entertainment industry, rising from a middle-class upbringing in Philadelphia to becoming one of Hollywood’s most recognisable stars. One of his most memorable motivational lines comes from his 2013 science-fiction film ‘After Earth’, where his character reflects on the difference between genuine danger and the fear created by the mind.The quote from the famed actor reads, "Fear is not real. It is a product of thoughts you create. Do not misunderstand me; danger is very real. But fear is a choice.”What does Will Smith’s quote about fear mean?The motivational quote comes from ‘After Earth’, in which Will Smith played Cypher Raige alongside his son Jaden Smith, who portrayed his character’s son, Kitai. In the film, Cypher shares the words while explaining how fear can affect the way people respond to dangerous situations. At its core, the quote draws a distinction between danger and fear. Danger can be an external reality, while fear can be shaped by the thoughts and interpretations that a person attaches to a situation.Fear can often emerge before an event has even happened. People may worry about a relationship, a career decision, a business opportunity or taking an important step towards a personal goal. In such situations, the mind can create possible outcomes and repeatedly focus on what could go wrong, making an imagined scenario feel increasingly real.Smith’s quote does not suggest that genuine danger should be ignored. Instead, it emphasises the importance of recognising the difference between an actual threat and the fear generated by anticipation, uncertainty or self-doubt. The broader message is about regaining perspective when anxiety or apprehension begins to take over. Rather than allowing fear to dictate every decision, the quote encourages people to focus on what is within their control, trust their abilities and deal with the situation in front of them.Will Smith’s early life and rise to fameWillard Carroll Smith Jr. was born on September 25, 1968, in West Philadelphia. He grew up in a middle-class family, with his father working as an engineer and his mother as a school board administrator. From a young age, Smith earned the nickname “Prince” because of his charm and ability to talk his way out of difficult situations. The nickname later became part of his stage persona. Smith’s first major step into the entertainment industry came through music rather than acting. He became friends with DJ Jazzy Jeff, and the two formed the hip-hop duo DJ Jazzy Jeff & The Fresh Prince. Their debut album, ‘Rock the House’, was released in 1987 and eventually went gold. Their second album, ‘He's the DJ, I'm the Rapper’, arrived in 1988 and became a major success. That same year, Smith won a Grammy for Best Rap Performance, becoming one of the early recipients of the award after the category was introduced.Will Smith faced financial difficulties before becoming a Hollywood starDespite his success in music, Smith later faced significant financial problems. His career took a major turn when record executive Quincy Jones helped develop the sitcom ‘The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air’, which became Smith’s breakthrough in television. The show provided him with regular income while he dealt with financial problems involving the IRS. Looking back at that period during an interview with ‘60 Minutes’, Smith spoke about the financial pressure he experienced despite appearing successful to the outside world.“For the first three years of The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air, the IRS was taking 70 percent of every check, and after the third year, I got back to zero. It's terrible to have that kind of success and have to quietly be broke,” he said.From ‘Bad Boys’ to Hollywood stardomSmith made his major breakthrough on the big screen with ‘Bad Boys’, which helped establish him as a Hollywood leading man. He subsequently became one of the industry’s biggest stars, appearing in a wide range of commercially successful films. His filmography includes ‘Independence Day’, ‘Men in Black’, ‘Enemy of the State’, ‘Wild Wild West’, ‘The Pursuit of Happyness’, ‘I, Robot’, ‘Hancock’, ‘I Am Legend’, ‘Hitch’, ‘Bright’ and ‘Emancipation’, among others.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more.
